content: José Silvia is affiliated with the National Cancer Institute in the USA, representing the Americas. Julia Gage, also from the National Cancer Institute in the USA, contributes to the same region. Patti Gravitt, from the Center for Global Health at the National Cancer Institute, USA, focuses on global health initiatives in the Americas. Rolando Herrero is associated with the Costa Rican Agency for Biomedical Research, contributing to cancer research in the Americas. Ebony Johnson represents communities of women living with HIV in the USA, focusing on advocacy and health equity in the Americas. Mauricio Maza, from Basic Health International in El Salvador, works on health initiatives in the Americas. Raul Murillo, based at Hospital Universitario San Ignacio in Colombia, contributes to cancer research and treatment in the Americas. Kelle Moley, representing the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, focuses on reproductive health technologies in the USA and the Americas. Gina Ogilvie, from BC Women’s Hospital and Health Centre in Canada, contributes to women’s health in the Americas. Maria Alejandra Picconi, from the HPV Reference Laboratory at the National Institute for Infectious Diseases in Argentina, specializes in HPV research in the Americas. Leeya Pinder, from the University of Washington in the USA, contributes to public health research in the Americas. Veronica Reis, representing Jhpiego in the USA, focuses on global health initiatives in the Americas. Gracia Violetta Ross Quiroga, from the Bolivian Network of People Living with HIV/AIDS, advocates for HIV/AIDS care and support in Bolivia and the Americas. Vikrant Sahasrabuddhe, from the National Cancer Institute in the USA, contributes to cancer research in the Americas. Rose Slavkovsky and Kerry Thomson, both from PATH in the USA, work on health innovation and implementation in the Americas. Nicolas Wentzensen, from the National Cancer Institute in the USA, focuses on cancer research in the Eastern Mediterranean region. Waqar Muhammad Atif, from Aga Khan University Hospital in Pakistan, contributes to cancer care in the Eastern Mediterranean. Ali Ghanbari-Motlagh, from the Ministry of Health in Iran, works on public health initiatives in the Eastern Mediterranean. Tarek Hashem, from Menoufia University in Egypt, contributes to medical research in the Eastern Mediterranean. Laia Bruni, from the Catalan Institute of Oncology in Spain, focuses on cancer research in Europe. Marie-Claude Boily, from Imperial College London in the United Kingdom, specializes in epidemiology and public health in Europe. Joanna Cain, representing the International Federation of Obstetrics and Gynecology (FIGO) in the United Kingdom, contributes to women’s health initiatives in Europe. Helen Kelly, from the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine in the United Kingdom, focuses on global health research in Europe. Anne Mackie, from Public Health England, works on screening and quality assurance services in the United Kingdom. Patrick Petignat, from Hôpitaux Universitaires de Genève in Switzerland, contributes to cancer research in Europe. Walter Prendiville, from the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC) in France, focuses on global cancer research. Peter Sasieni and Julie Torode, both from King’s College London in the United Kingdom, contribute to cancer prevention and public health research in Europe. Neerja Bhatla, from the All India Institute of Medical Sciences in India, works on cancer research in South-East Asia. Wachara Eamratsameekool, from Phanomphrai Community Hospital in Thailand, contributes to public health initiatives in South-East Asia. Ashrafun Nessa, from Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujib Medical University in Bangladesh, focuses on women’s health in South-East Asia. Myint Myint Thinn, from Central Women’s Hospital in Myanmar, contributes to maternal health in South-East Asia. Bayarsaikhan Luvsandorj, from the National Cancer Center of Mongolia, works on cancer research in the Western Pacific. Fanghui Zhao, from the China Cancer Institute, contributes to cancer prevention and treatment in China and the Western Pacific. Nancy Santesso, from McMaster University in Canada, provides expertise in guideline development, systematic reviews, and clinical epidemiology. Marc Arbyn, from the Belgian Cancer Centre, leads systematic reviews on HPV triage strategies. Karen Canfell, from the Daffodil Centre in Australia, leads modeling work for cervical cancer screening and prevention, including for women living with HIV. Megan Smith and Susan Yuill, also from the Daffodil Centre, contribute to model development and evidence reviews. Owen Demke, from the Clinton Health Access Initiative in Rwanda, and Cindy Gauvreau, from the Hospital for Sick Children/University of Toronto in Canada, provide costing expertise for health initiatives. Benjamin Anderson, from the University of Washington in the USA, and Hans Berkhof, from Vrije Universiteit in the Netherlands, serve as observers in global health initiatives. Michelle Chevalier, from PEPFAR in the USA, and Smiljka de Lussigny, from Unitaid in Switzerland, contribute to HIV/AIDS programs. Danielle Engel, from the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) in the USA, and Eduardo Franco, from McGill University in Canada, focus on cancer epidemiology and reproductive health. Maribel Almonte Pacheco, from the Department of Noncommunicable Diseases at WHO, and Paul Bloem, from the Department of Immunization, Vaccines, and Biologicals, contribute to global health programs. Nathalie Broutet, from the Department of Sexual and Reproductive Health, and Shona Dalal, from the Department of Global HIV, Hepatitis, and STIs, focus on reproductive health and infectious diseases. Ajay Rangaraj leads the development of clinical algorithms for women living with HIV, supported by experts such as Patti Gravitt, Nancy Santesso, and others. These efforts aim to improve screening, triage, and treatment strategies for cervical cancer and other health conditions.
